Policy.description: How a worker admits one offloaded unit: a machine offers itself (headroom) when its smallest unit fits (`smallestMegabytes`), the free memory it reports is what a unit may still take above its floor, and a unit is admitted when its own predicted peak fits into that beside the part of their peaks the running units have not grown into yet. Raised memory pressure (`warn`) alone refuses only units above `warnMaximumMegabytes` and every unit while swap is growing; critical pressure refuses all. How many units a machine lends while its readiness stage runs is decided by measured memory alone (the stage keeps its own reserve through its claim): a fixed count of one unit per stage left every worker whose stage read for hours unable to take a component final although it had the memory.
